register.level: harried, sleepless mother guarding her eggs: shrieking accusation alternating with a sobbing litany of grievance
register.summary: She has decided Alice is a serpent and no evidence will move her. She speaks at, not to, Alice ('without attending to her', ch005-p53): long complaints built on repetition (I've tried …, and I've tried …, and I've tried …; just as I'd …, and just as I was …), shrieked accusations (Serpent!), and contemptuous dismissal (A likely story indeed!). Her logic bends every fact to her fear (if little girls eat eggs, they're a kind of serpent). Per SUP-002 (amended BIB-0027) a photoreal CGI pigeon, agitated wing-beats punctuating the shrieks, defending an unseen nest.

examples.text: I've tried the roots of trees, and I've tried banks, and I've tried hedges, but those serpents! There's no pleasing them!
I don't believe it, but if they do, why then they're a kind of serpent, that's all I can say.

sentence_style.length: mixed: a shrieked single word (Serpent!) against long run-on complaints of 20-30 words; mean 21.2 words over 10 lines

patterns.rule: Accusation by epithet, shrieked and repeated regardless of reply (Serpent! / Serpent, I say again! / Ugh, Serpent! / You're a serpent).

examples.text: …they must needs come wriggling down from the sky! Ugh, Serpent!

patterns.rule: Grievance litany: anaphora and accumulation (I've tried …, and I've tried …; just as I'd …, and just as I was …; As if it wasn't trouble enough …, but I must …), ending in an exclamation of despair.

examples.text: I've tried the roots of trees, and I've tried banks, and I've tried hedges, but those serpents! There's no pleasing them!
As if it wasn't trouble enough hatching the eggs, but I must be on the look-out for serpents night and day!

patterns.rule: Contemptuous disbelief and dismissal (A likely story indeed! / I don't believe it / there's no use denying it / I can see you're trying to invent something / Well, be off, then!).

examples.text: A likely story indeed! … No, no! You're a serpent; and there's no use denying it.
Well! What are you? I can see you're trying to invent something!

patterns.rule: Nesting-mother vocabulary: eggs, hatching, the highest tree, the look-out night and day, not a wink of sleep these three weeks.

examples.text: Why, I haven't had a wink of sleep these three weeks!
You're looking for eggs, I know that well enough;
And just as I'd taken the highest tree in the wood…

address.self: I (the long-suffering sufferer at the centre of every sentence)
address.to_alice: Serpent! as a term of address; otherwise 'you' in accusations; never 'child', 'little girl' as an address

examples.text: …what does it matter to me whether you're a little girl or a serpent?

forbidden_words.regex: \b(sorry|I beg your pardon|forgive me|I believe you|you're right|my mistake|never mind|don't worry)\b
forbidden_words.reason: she never accepts Alice's account (ch005-d0060, d0062); a concession would break the scene's logic
0 of 10 lines are courteous; she speaks at Alice, not to her

drift.change: Arc within one scene: shriek (ch005-d0049) → sob-laden grievance (d0051-d0056) → cold contempt and 'logic' (d0058-d0063) → sulky dismissal as she settles back on the nest (d0065, 'in a sulky tone').

backtest_markers.regex: \b(I've tried|no pleasing|nothing seems to suit|as if it wasn't|just as I)\b
\b(a likely story|I don't believe|no use denying|trying to invent|be off|what are you\?)

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test (shared yardstick with pb1 and 01-story/dialogue-rewrite): a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb2/result.json#backtest_method
